title: GOP Friction Escalates: Ted Cruz Slams 'Insecure' JD Vance in Spat Over 2028 Ambitions
snippet: Texas Senator Ted Cruz hit back at Vice President JD Vance, dismissing claims he is distracted by a 2028 White House run and calling Vance's critiques 'political bomb-throwing.'
content:
Tensions within the Republican Party spilled into the open this weekend as Texas Sen. Ted Cruz fired back at Vice President JD Vance, dismissing accusations that he is prioritizing a 2028 presidential bid over the upcoming midterm elections.

Speaking in a phone interview Saturday, Cruz labeled Vance's recent critiques as the actions of a political rival feeling vulnerable.

"In my experience, people engage in political bomb-throwing when they're feeling insecure," Cruz said. "So he's welcome to make whatever comments he likes. I'm going to keep focusing on the midterms and helping us win on Election Day in the next 30 days."

Early Jockeying for 2028

The public rift erupted following an NBC News interview on Thursday, in which Vance suggested Cruz was prematurely laying the groundwork for a White House run rather than concentrating on helping Republicans retain Congress.

"It is really obvious to me that, at this very moment, Ted Cruz is running for president," Vance said during the broadcast. "At this moment, I’m not. I’m trying to help elect Republicans. That’s what I’m going to keep on doing."

Vance is broadly viewed as a primary frontrunner for the 2028 GOP nomination, but Cruz has resisted stepping aside. In August, Cruz hinted he might throw his hat in the ring again, telling reporters he expected to "certainly be part of the discussion."

Defending the Trail Record

Cruz forcefully rejected Vance's assertion that he is neglecting current party battles. Highlighting a grueling campaign itinerary, Cruz pointed to recent stump speeches in Georgia, Iowa, Nebraska, and South Carolina, alongside scheduled stops in Alaska, Florida, and North Carolina.

"Over the last 10 years, there's no Republican in the country who has campaigned for more Senate candidates, more House candidates, more gubernatorial candidates than I have, and this year will be no exception," Cruz said.

The Texas senator also noted the irony in Vance's sharp words, pointing out that he aggressively stumped for Vance during his 2022 Senate campaign in Ohio.

"Indeed, ironically, I spent a full day on the road with JD Vance, campaigning with him when he was running for Senate in Ohio," Cruz added. "I was very glad he won that race. I was very glad to help him."

A spokesperson for Vance did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding Cruz's latest remarks. Both leaders remain actively engaged on the campaign trail, with Vance making stops in Texas, Florida, and Alaska this week.
